hypothesis: The advisory public default competes with the actual delivered leader plan: varying the default at fixed plan changes follower choices, and removing the default increases sensitivity to live versus flipped messages.
bundle_sampling: Uniform shuffle seed 261016043 of 24 lane-name/order/value descriptors; first 12. No claim of new semantic domains.
independence_unit: descriptor bundle, not leaders or individual choices
primary_outcomes: within-bundle follower A/B change under default A versus B at fixed leader/channel
within-bundle follower A/B change under live versus flipped channel at each default
invariants: default is explicitly advisory and changes no permissions, requirements or lane quality
actual model-generated leader choice fixed across follower interventions
same follower seed and greedy decoding
analysis: Full 18-cell table; primary fractions averaged within the 12 descriptor bundles. All failures retained. Descriptive estimates only; no message-level independence claims.
exclusion_policy: None; invalid source/choice recorded and scored unsuccessful.
stopping_rule: One named diagnostic only; no effect-driven expansion or prompt changes. Original v1 readiness failure remains unchanged.
budget: Within the existing exp4 pilot $10 and workflow $60 caps. Shared broker only.
